Second-Gen Polestar 2 Gets Unofficially Imagined Based on Formula 2030 Concept, Lacks a Rear Window
8 photos
Photo: sugardesign_1 / Instagram
Polestar Automotive Holding UK PLC, known simply as Polestar , is the premium sports Swedish automotive manufacturer crafted as the brainchild of both Volvo Cars and its Chinese parent company Geely.
Polestar, which is traded publicly on the Nasdaq stock exchange, is headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden, and mainly sells automobiles across North America, Europe, and the Asia Pacific regions. It was established as an independent brand in 2017, and the first model they created was dubbed simply Polestar 1, a plug-in hybrid grand tourer made in China in just 1,500 units.
Currently, the roster is composed of Polestar 2 , 3, 4 as a coupe or SUV, and the Polestar 5. There will be many new introductions in the near future: the Polestar 2’s fresh successor will launch next year, followed by the Polestar 7 compact SUV coming in 2028, and the Polestar 6 roadster as a hero model further down the line.
The first-generation Polestar 2 was the company’s first mass-produced model, and earlier this month ended production after more than 200k units – the brand’s Tesla Model 3 rival will get a successor in 2027, most likely continuing its legacy as a five-door liftback sedan proposition.
Recently, Polestar unveiled a fancy prototype dubbed the Polestar Formula 2030 Concept, a model that looks like a hot hatchback or something that Saab would create if they were still around, and comes with coach rear doors to make it worth our attention.
However, the company says it won’t be produced, and instead various styling elements will make their way to the new models it has cooking, like the next-gen Polestar 2 and a future Polestar 7 model. Well, if you can’t wait to see the Formula 2030 translated into a more serious model, the parallel universes of vehicular CGI will come to your aid via the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
More precisely, Sugar Chow, the virtual artist better known as " sugardesign_1 " on social media, has decided to CGI-present his vision for the all-new, second-gen Polestar 2 liftback – and it’s fully inspired by the Formula 2030, quite obviously.
The pixel master adapts the concept’s design features into a series-production model, keeping the split headlights and DRLs along with the fresh bumper style. But the profile is of a classic liftback now, and while the rear reuses the concept’s slim LED taillights and the bumper with cutouts and integrated diffuser, it’s also wackier now because it lacks a standard rear window.
Naturally, the all-new Polestar 2 would continue as an electric-only model, this time around produced on a dedicated EV platform that’s not shared with combustion models. So, what do you think – yay or nay for this unofficial, hypothetical design project? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sugarchow (@sugardesign_1)
